chapters.title: Welcome tour
chapters.summary: Ten stops around the Workbench, ending at this checklist

steps.title: Everything on one rail
steps.body: Every tab lives on this rail, in three groups: what reaches you and where you work, then what you keep and do, then your brain and its agents. Hover an icon for its name.

steps.title: Pulse is your home
steps.body: Click **Pulse**: a one-paragraph briefing, what needs you, and ten areas at a glance. The mark at the top of the rail always brings you back here.

steps.title: Sessions
steps.body: Click **Sessions**: run {host} in a workspace turn by turn, follow and resume each conversation, and ask questions about your vault in Vault chat.

steps.title: Code, a terminal deck
steps.body: Click **Code**: start {host} or a shell in any workspace, keep several running side by side, and write longer prompts in the composer. ⌘T starts one from any tab.

steps.title: Brain, your memory
steps.body: Click **Brain**: what your sessions learned, to review and keep; a library of every memory; and what each new session starts with. Keeping it tidy keeps your agents accurate.

steps.title: Spaces, your projects
steps.body: Click **Spaces**: one row per workspace folder, with its status, last session, files and history, and a button to pick the work back up where you left it.

steps.title: Routines run for you
steps.body: Click **Routines**: prompts, commands and duties that run on a schedule on your Mac, with when each runs next and whether its last run worked.

steps.title: Your Chief of Staff
steps.body: Click **Proposals**. Your Chief of Staff is an agent that runs duties for you: it writes the briefing on Pulse and files proposals here for you to approve or reject. Nothing it proposes changes without you.

steps.title: Find anything with ⌘K
steps.body: ⌘K searches workspace files, memories, runs, agents, skills and actions from any tab. ⌘P lists every command, and the + below captures a memory.

steps.title: Help is here
steps.body: Take this tour again, tour the tab you are on, see what's new, or open your Getting started checklist. Click **Done** to open the checklist now.

chapters.title: Notifications
chapters.summary: Read what your agents and routines post, filter it, and act on it

steps.title: Unread at a glance
steps.body: Notifications heads the rail. Its badge counts the unread items and turns rose while a breaking one is unread, so you can tell from any tab that something urgent arrived.

steps.title: Your inbox
steps.body: What agents, routines and duties post with aos notify lands here. The count shows unread and total, and **Mark all read** appears while anything is unread. {cmd:notifications} reads and clears them from {host}.

steps.title: Unread, All, Archived
steps.body: Unread shows what you have not opened, All adds what you have read, and Archived holds what you put away. Click **All** to see everything.

steps.title: Filter by level
steps.body: The level chips narrow the list to breaking, alert, edition or info; click one again to clear it. When more than one agent posts, the sender menu narrows it to one of them.

steps.title: The list
steps.body: Newest first, each row shows an unread dot, its level, the title, who posted it and how long ago. Click a row to read it beside the list; opening an item marks it read.

steps.title: Read and act
steps.body: The open item, section by section. A button marked ❯_ opens a {host} session in Code running the skill it names; ▲ and ▼ record what you want more or less of. Links below mark it read, archive it or open its note.

chapters.title: Pulse
chapters.summary: Your home: the briefing, what needs you, and every area at a glance

steps.title: Pulse is Home
steps.body: Pulse opens first, and the mark at the top of the rail brings you back here. Its badge counts what needs you and turns rose when something is broken.

steps.title: Your briefing
steps.body: Where things stand, in one paragraph. When your Chief of Staff has written one recently you read theirs; otherwise Pulse composes it from the facts. Each highlighted phrase opens the area it names.

steps.title: Quick commands
steps.body: **/scan** and **/reflect-week** run now, **/brain** opens BRAIN.md, the capture commands open a form, and **/wrap** and **/ask-brain** copy the command to paste into {host}. Hover one to see what it does.

steps.title: Rescan and act
steps.body: When the vault was last scanned, a button to rescan it, and one to write the briefing now (or turn it on). Below them, a button for each of the top one or two things that need you.

steps.title: Ten areas, one glance
steps.body: Each tile counts one area and shows the rows that fit. Click a tile to open its area in a popup: the list on its left switches areas, ↑↓ walks it, and Esc closes it.

steps.title: What needs you
steps.body: Everything waiting on you, most urgent first: what is broken, then decisions, stale work and reading. Each row's button acts in place, or jumps to where it is handled when it ends in →.

steps.title: System health
steps.body: Errors, warnings and notes from the last vault scan, with a light for each pipeline and routine. Open it for the issues, the Fix Queue of one-click fixes, and a link to the System drawer.

steps.title: Decisions waiting
steps.body: Proposals, team gates, flags and feedback drafts that wait on your call, led by the one waiting longest. In its popup each opens its review: a {host} session, Agent Teams, or the Brain tab.

steps.title: Brain at a glance
steps.body: Memories written today and since you last looked. Its numbers jump into the Brain tab: memories to review, feedback drafts, and BRAIN.md against its budget. Pulse summarises; Brain acts.

chapters.title: Code
chapters.summary: Start, find and switch terminals, grouped by where they run

steps.title: Start a terminal
steps.body: **New** starts the host you used last; ⌘T does the same from any tab. Its second line says where it will run and, for an agent, with which model and access.

steps.title: Choose host and place
steps.body: ▾ or ⇧⌘T opens the menu: start any host or a shell now, pick a workspace or name a new one, set what the agent may do, and see the exact command first. ⌥⌘3 opens a shell, ⇧⌘N a new workspace.

steps.title: Claude Code in one key
steps.body: ⌥⌘1 starts **Claude Code** from any tab, whatever host you used last; the ▾ menu lists it under Start now with where it will run.

steps.title: Codex in one key
steps.body: ⌥⌘2 starts **Codex** from any tab, whatever host you used last; the ▾ menu lists it under Start now with where it will run.

steps.title: Filter terminals
steps.body: Type here to narrow the list by a terminal's title, its place or what started it. Clear it to see them all again.

steps.title: Terminals by place
steps.body: Grouped by where they run: workspaces and Scratch first, then the vault and other folders. Hover a group for its + to start one there. Rows show host, title and how it ended; ⇧⌘] and ⇧⌘[ step through.

steps.title: Open and ended
steps.body: Counts the open and ended terminals. **Clear ended** removes the finished ones, and ⇧⌘W closes the selected terminal, asking first while an agent still runs in it.

steps.title: The selected terminal
steps.body: Shows where the selected terminal runs and its host, model and access. Click the place to start an agent or a shell there, link a code folder or copy the path; an ended agent offers Restart and Resume.

steps.title: The terminal
steps.body: The selected terminal runs here, and you type straight into it. Links it prints open in your browser or on their Workbench tab, and ⌘F finds text in it, scrollback included.

steps.title: Write longer messages
steps.body: Under a running terminal, the composer takes longer messages: ⏎ sends, ⇧⏎ adds a line, @ picks a file, / lists the agent's commands, Snippets keeps prompts you reuse. ⌘L jumps there.

chapters.title: Sessions
chapters.summary: Run agent sessions in your workspaces and ask questions about your vault

steps.title: Your sessions
steps.body: A session runs {host} in one of your workspace folders, turn by turn. Select one here to follow it on the right, where **Review changes** shows what it changed and lets you commit it.

steps.title: Start a session
steps.body: Opens a composer: pick the workspace, what the agent may do, and the host, model and effort, then write the prompt. Type / for the host's commands and press ⌘↵ to send.

steps.title: Vault chat
steps.body: Click **Vault** to ask questions about your notes. It is always in the list, read only, and keeps your recent questions and answers.

steps.title: Sessions by workspace
steps.body: Grouped by workspace folder, newest first; the dot shows the host and ● a running turn. Reply in one to resume it on the same host. Opened from a workspace, the list shows only its sessions until **Show all**.

steps.title: Today's session spend
steps.body: What today's session turns have cost against the daily cap in Settings. The bar warns at 80%, and once the cap is reached no new turn starts until tomorrow.

steps.title: What answers you
steps.body: The line beside **Vault** names the route your next question takes, such as the host and model. Your past questions and their answers show below it.

steps.title: Ask about your notes
steps.body: Type a question and press ⌘↵. It finds the most relevant notes and memories in your vault, and a model answers from them; today's Vault spend shows underneath.

steps.title: Always read only
steps.body: Vault questions run without tools, so they never change a file. In a session this chip is a menu: **Read only**, **Edit files** (the default) or **Edit and run commands**.

steps.title: Host, model and effort
steps.body: Choose what answers. With background work on this Mac, **This Mac** (the local model, free) answers by default; pick a host, model and effort for a question when you want one. Each question can use any ready host, and your pick is remembered. A new session has the same chip, and once it starts its host stays fixed.

chapters.title: Sessions ▸ History
chapters.summary: Every past Claude Code and Codex session on this Mac, by day, with Resume

steps.title: History
steps.body: Click **History**: every Claude Code and Codex session this Mac has a record of, whichever host ran it, even one that is off now. It reads the scan's index, never a transcript.

steps.title: Past sessions by day
steps.body: Newest first, each with its host, time and workspace, and a one-line summary once the history import has digested it. Type to filter. **Resume** reopens one in a Code terminal on its own host, when that host is on and signed in.

chapters.title: To-Do
chapters.summary: Add, sort and tick off the to-dos kept in TODO.md

steps.title: Today at a glance
steps.body: How many to-dos are open, overdue and due today. The To-Do badge on the rail counts overdue plus today, so you see it from any tab.

steps.title: The file behind it
steps.body: Your to-dos live in TODO.md in your vault, in Tasks-plugin syntax. **open TODO.md** opens it in a tab, and {cmd:todo} in a session adds to the same file.

steps.title: Add a to-do
steps.body: Type it and press Enter or **+ add**. Pick a priority and a due date beside it, or write #tags and Tasks priority and date markers inline.

steps.title: Filter by tag
steps.body: Every #tag on an open to-do gets a chip. Click one to show only those to-dos, or **all** to clear the filter. A tag on a row filters the same way.

steps.title: Grouped by when
steps.body: Open to-dos fall into Overdue, Today, Upcoming and Someday (no due date), highest priority first, then by date. Late ones say how many days late.

steps.title: Work a to-do
steps.body: Tick the box when it's done. Double-click the text to edit the whole line. The priority button cycles high, medium, low and none, the date picker sets the due date, and ✕ deletes it.

steps.title: Done this week
steps.body: Ticked to-dos stay in TODO.md. Click here to show what you finished in the last seven days; untick one to reopen it.

chapters.title: Spaces
chapters.summary: Pick a project back up: its status, last session, files and history

steps.title: Your workspaces
steps.body: Your project folders under workspaces/, grouped Pinned, Active, Stalled and Idle. Each row shows status, git, sessions per host, last activity and the next step. Filter at the top; click a row to open it.

steps.title: Make a new space
steps.body: **New** makes a workspace folder: blank, a git repo, or a clone from GitHub. It is pinned to the top of the list and opens in Code with the agent or terminal you pick.

steps.title: Sessions outside workspaces
steps.body: Folders where agent sessions ran outside every workspace. Open the list to adopt a folder into a workspace (nothing moves), link it as a workspace's code folder, or hide it.

steps.title: Status and pin
steps.body: The pill says how the workspace is going; **auto** means it is worked out from sessions and commits. Click it to set Active, Paused or Done in workspace.md, or go back to automatic. The pin keeps it on top.

steps.title: Pick up the work
steps.body: **Resume in Code** reopens the last session in a Code terminal here, or says why it can't; with no session yet it reads **Start in Code**. The arrow offers a new session, a terminal, or Sessions.

steps.title: More actions
steps.body: Rename, set status, link a code folder, draft workspace.md from the folder's files, copy the path, or archive. Archive moves it to workspaces/_archive/, and Restore brings it back.

steps.title: Where you left off
steps.body: **last** is the newest session and the line Resume types; **now** and **next** come from the handoff, plan or workspace.md; **read** is a one-line insight, and ↻ writes a fresh one.

steps.title: Overview and Files
steps.body: **Overview** shows the summary, objectives and documents. Click **Files** to see the folder as one tree, each file with its description.

steps.title: Files and their map
steps.body: Each file with its description from the workspace map. Filter by path or description; **NEW** and **CHANGED** mark what the map hasn't caught up with, and **Describe** fills in the new ones. Click a file to preview it.

steps.title: History
steps.body: Sessions from every host and the folder's commits, newest first; filter with All, Sessions or Commits. **Resume** on a row reopens that thread, or says why it can't.

steps.title: Linked work
steps.body: To-dos tagged #ws/ with this workspace's name, plus proposals and memory notes that name it, each saying how it links. **+ to-do** adds a tagged to-do; **Link to-dos…** tags ones that mention it.

chapters.title: Files
chapters.summary: Browse, search and tidy every file in your vault

steps.title: Your whole vault
steps.body: Every file in your vault, as a tree you can browse, search and tidy. The count is how many files it lists.

steps.title: Make a note
steps.body: **+ note** asks for a folder and a name, checks the path as you type, then creates the Markdown note and opens it in a tab.

steps.title: Open any file
steps.body: **open…** (⌘O) finds a file from a few letters of its path, Markdown first, and opens it.

steps.title: Search your notes
steps.body: Type to search inside your notes: each matching line shows with the hit highlighted, and a click opens that note. Esc clears it, and ⇧⌘F jumps here from anywhere.

steps.title: Search more than notes
steps.body: Tick **all text files** to search code, JSON, YAML, CSV and other text files too, not only Markdown. Very large files are skipped.

steps.title: The vault tree
steps.body: Folders come first. Click a folder to open it, a note to open it in a tab. Hover a row for ✎ rename, → move and ✕ Trash; a folder's + makes a note in it.

chapters.title: Routines
chapters.summary: Schedule recurring prompts, commands and duties, and see how they ran

steps.title: Recurring work
steps.body: Routines are jobs that run on a schedule, one file each in brain/routines. The count shows how many are on out of the total.

steps.title: Create a routine
steps.body: **+ new** opens the editor: a name, the kind (prompt, command or duty), a cron schedule with its next three fire times previewed, and the prompt or command to run.

steps.title: Apply schedules
steps.body: **apply schedules** has the runtime register each enabled routine's schedule on your Mac. A banner appears here when a routine changed since the last apply.

steps.title: Your routines
steps.body: Each row shows the kind, the cadence in words, the next fire, the last run with its exit code and cost, and a health chip: ok, off, stale, missed, failed or invalid.

steps.title: Run, pause or edit
steps.body: ▶ runs a routine now. **on**/**off** enables or disables it and re-applies schedules. ✎ edits it; a guarded duty belongs to the Chief of Staff and asks before its schedule or body changes.

steps.title: Outside the runtime
steps.body: Schedules the runtime doesn't run, shown read-only: launchd jobs listed in routines.externalLabels, the vault's Git backup timer if it has one, and routines your session hosts keep themselves.

steps.title: Claude Code cloud routines
steps.body: The claude rows are a snapshot of your Claude Code cloud routines, dated here. Run /routines cloud in a Claude Code session to update it; edit them at claude.ai.

steps.title: Codex Automations
steps.body: The codex rows are your Codex Automations, re-read from the Codex app when this tab loads and the copy is over ten minutes old. **refresh** re-reads them now; edit them in Codex.

chapters.title: Proposals
chapters.summary: Read the Chief of Staff's proposals, backlog and past decisions

steps.title: What's waiting
steps.body: Your Chief of Staff files proposals: changes to approve or reject, and ideas to accept into a backlog or dismiss. The rail badge counts the pending ones.

steps.title: Decide in a review
steps.body: The **Review** button opens a terminal in Code, in the vault, and starts the persona-flag-closer review in {host}. You decide each proposal there; this tab only reads.

steps.title: How you've decided
steps.body: Over the last 28 days, the share of changes you approved and of ideas you accepted, counted from the ledger. It shows how well the proposals fit you.

steps.title: Pending proposals
steps.body: Proposals waiting for your decision. Click a group heading to fold it away; Backlog and History below fold the same way.

steps.title: Read a proposal
steps.body: Each row names what it would change, its kind and its age. **confirmed** counts the days a recheck still found the problem; ⚠ marks a proposal missing parts. Click it to read it.

steps.title: The reading pane
steps.body: The selected proposal opens here: what it needs from you, What, Why and Risk, the premises it rests on, and links to its page in the browser and to its file.

steps.title: Accepted ideas
steps.body: Ideas you accepted wait here, newest first, from persona/backlog.md. Click one to read its notes and open its page or the backlog file.

steps.title: Every decision
steps.body: Recent outcomes from the ledger, newest first: ✓ approved or applied, ✗ rejected or regressed, ◇ accepted, – dismissed or dropped. **page ↗** opens a proposal's page.

chapters.title: Brain
chapters.summary: Everything your agents remember, in one hub with five modes

steps.title: Your brain at a glance
steps.body: Brain holds what your agents wrote down. This line counts your live memories, patterns and reflections and, while sessions keep adding them, about how many a day.

steps.title: Search the brain
steps.body: Type to search titles and bodies. Brain switches to Library and filters as you type. **⌘F** jumps here from anywhere in Brain, and Esc clears it.

steps.title: Capture a memory
steps.body: Write a memory by hand: pick its type, give it a title and a body, and it is saved with the others and listed in MEMORY.md. Handy for a rule you want every session to know.

steps.title: Five modes
steps.body: Brain works in five modes. Their counts show what waits for review, your live memories, how full BRAIN.md is and what Health can fix. ←/→ move between them.

steps.title: Review
steps.body: What your sessions wrote, one session at a time. Keep, edit, merge, archive or pin each new memory so the brain stays accurate. Its count is how many wait for you.

steps.title: Library
steps.body: Find and read anything Brain holds: memories, feedback drafts, patterns and reflections, with filters, a reader and what links to each. Its count is your live memories.

steps.title: Bootstrap
steps.body: What every new {host} session starts with: BRAIN.md and your working memory against their budgets. Its count is how full BRAIN.md is.

steps.title: Map
steps.body: Your memories as graphify's communities: groups that link to each other, each memory's neighbours and the whole graph. With the graph off, it tells you how to turn it on.

steps.title: Health
steps.body: The brain's shape in six tiles, with the fixes: duplicates to compare, hygiene fixes that preview first and memories nobody uses. Its count is what it can fix now.

chapters.title: Review
chapters.summary: Keep, merge or archive what each session wrote

steps.title: Four review queues
steps.body: **By session** lists what each session wrote, **Drafts** holds rules drafted from your corrections, **Duplicates** pairs memories that read alike, and **Older than 30d** is the backlog.

steps.title: Open By session
steps.body: Click **By session** to review one session's memories at a time. This week's sessions come first; older ones fold under Earlier.

steps.title: Sessions that wrote memories
steps.body: Each row is one session: its title, its host, how many memories are new, and a pill when some look like ones you already have. The bars show each memory's type. Pick a row to review it.

steps.title: Keep the new ones
steps.body: Keeps every memory in this session that looks new, in one go (**⇧K**). Ones that look like a memory you already have stay for you to compare. The ⋯ button keeps or archives them all.

steps.title: One card per memory
steps.body: Each card shows the memory's type, title and description. A **looks like** pill means it reads like one you already have. Double-click a card, or press ⏎, to read it in Library.

steps.title: Act on a memory
steps.body: **Keep** marks it reviewed, **Edit** opens the note, **Merge** compares it with its look-alike, **Archive** retires it and **Pin** puts it in BRAIN.md. Restore in Library undoes an archive.

steps.title: Review from the keyboard
steps.body: ↑↓ move between cards and every action has a key (K, E, M, A, P), so you can clear a whole session without the mouse.

steps.title: Nothing is deleted
steps.body: Reviewing deletes no memory: kept ones leave this list and archived ones can be restored. When an old backlog piles up, **Mark everything before…** marks it reviewed in one step, after showing how many.

chapters.title: Library
chapters.summary: Find, read and tidy every memory, draft, pattern and reflection

steps.title: What to show
steps.body: Switch between your memories, feedback drafts waiting for approval, patterns and reflections. Each chip counts what it holds.

steps.title: Show memories
steps.body: Click **Memories** to list your live memories. The filters below work on memories only.

steps.title: Narrow with filters
steps.body: Filter by type, status and source, and by use once usage is logged. Status starts at live; pick archived or superseded to find a retired memory and restore it.

steps.title: The results
steps.body: Everything that matches the search and the filters, sorted by use when usage is logged, else newest first. Pick a row, or use ↑↓, to read it.

steps.title: Read it here
steps.body: The reader shows the file's title, type, status, where it came from and its full text, and says when a memory is part of BRAIN.md or was left out of it.

steps.title: Change one memory
steps.body: **Edit** opens the note. **Pin** puts it in BRAIN.md, **Status** sets it active, complete or paused, **Keep** marks it reviewed and **Archive** retires it (Restore brings it back). The last button opens it in the split pane.

steps.title: Its context
steps.body: How often agents used it in the last 30 days, what links to it, the memories that read close to it, and its history. After a merge, **Undo merge** shows here for up to 30 days.

chapters.title: Bootstrap
chapters.summary: See and steer what every new session starts with

steps.title: What sessions start with
steps.body: On the first prompt of every {host} session, BRAIN.md, your working memory and the last recall are injected. This page shows exactly what that is, and lets you trim it.

steps.title: The budgets
steps.body: BRAIN.md and SESSION.md against their token budgets, and how many recall hits the next first prompt carries. A bar turns amber when it is full or over budget.

steps.title: Who you are
steps.body: The first paragraph of your profile memory, so every session knows who it works for. **Open** shows it in Library, where you can edit it.

steps.title: Critical rules
steps.body: Your pinned memories, sent to every session. **Unpin** takes one out; **+ Pin a memory…** opens Library to pick another. Feedback rules work best here.

steps.title: Active context
steps.body: Your active projects, newest first, until the budget is full. **Mark complete** takes a finished one out. Projects that look shipped are flagged as suggestions only; nothing changes without your click.

steps.title: Last Session
steps.body: A short summary of your latest session, written every few turns by the session hooks so the next one can pick up where you left off. You don't edit it here.

steps.title: Recall preview
steps.body: Type a prompt and press ⏎ to see which memories recall would hand an agent for it, on either host. It changes no memory and logs no use.

steps.title: Working memory
steps.body: SESSION.md's lines to remember. Add one with {cmd:remember}; tag it #promote and the next {cmd:wrap} files it as a memory. It also says when a session ended without a wrap.

steps.title: The memory index
steps.body: MEMORY.md's size and anything wrong with it. Agents read it through tools, never at start-up. When it has problems, **Fix in Health →** takes you to the fixes.

chapters.title: Map
chapters.summary: See how your memories group into linked communities

steps.title: Communities view
steps.body: Click **Communities**. graphify groups memories that link to each other, and each group is named after its most-linked memory.

steps.title: Every community
steps.body: The communities with how many memories each holds, when graphify last built the graph, and what the map leaves out: index hubs, smaller groups and memories that link to nothing.

steps.title: One bubble per community
steps.body: A bubble's size is how many memories it holds; its ring is the share still waiting for review. Lines join communities that link. Click a bubble to see it.

steps.title: The community's card
steps.body: Its members, most linked first (click one to read it in Library), the communities it links to, and **Consolidate with AI…**, which asks a model for merges, archives and retitles after showing the cost.

steps.title: Around a memory
steps.body: Pick any memory in the map to see up to 12 of its neighbours on a ring, the line weight showing how many links join them.

steps.title: Every node
steps.body: The whole graph of memories as a force layout. Drag a node to pin it, ⌘-click to unpin it, scroll to zoom, and click a memory to open it in Library.

chapters.title: Health
chapters.summary: Spot duplicates, broken links and unused memories, and fix them

steps.title: Health at a glance
steps.body: Six tiles: duplicate pairs, memories to review, ones never used, how full BRAIN.md is, the size of MEMORY.md and broken links. Each says its state in words.

steps.title: Duplicates and clusters
steps.body: Pairs that read alike, closest first. **Compare** opens a pair in Review, **Merge with AI…** drafts one memory you approve before anything is written, and **Not duplicates** is remembered.

steps.title: Consolidation sweep
steps.body: One model call reads each memory's title, description and first lines and suggests merges, archives and retitles. You see the cost first, and nothing changes until you apply a suggestion.

steps.title: Hygiene fixes
steps.body: One-click fixes with no model: old source labels and types, descriptions kept only in MEMORY.md, index lines that are missing, misfiled or broken, and leftover drafts. Each previews its changes first.

steps.title: Dead weight
steps.body: Memories no agent injected, recalled or read lately. **Review the N** opens them in Library; **Archive the N shipped…** retires finished project notes after asking. With telemetry off, it says so.

chapters.title: Agent Teams
chapters.summary: Decide your teams' gates and follow their boards, members and channel

steps.title: Your agent teams
steps.body: A team is a lead agent and the seats it dispatches, working one board through stages. The count here, and the badge on the rail, show how many gates wait on you.

steps.title: Gates waiting on you
steps.body: When an item reaches a gate it stops until you decide. Every pending gate, from every team, waits here first, with how long it has waited, what it has spent and the lead's pitch.

steps.title: Set the phase budget
steps.body: The gate at a team's first stage sets the item's budget. Pick a preset or step it with − and +; it never goes below what is already spent, and **Approve** carries the amount.

steps.title: Approve or redirect
steps.body: **Approve** asks first, records your decision, then opens the lead in {host} to take the next step. **Redirect** opens the lead so you can say what should change.

steps.title: Pick a team
steps.body: Each chip is a team. A sub-team sits indented under its parent, a number counts its waiting gates, and **!** marks a TEAM.md that could not be read.

steps.title: Who is on the team
steps.body: Click **Roster** to see each member's provider and model, whether it is working, blocked, paused or idle, its current item and last run, and a ❯_ link to talk to it.

steps.title: Talk to the team
steps.body: Click **Interact** for the team's channel, filterable by item. A message you send goes to the lead, who reads it on its next step; **Talk to** starts the lead now.

steps.title: Change the seats
steps.body: Click **Manage** to pick each seat's provider, model and effort, pause the team or one member, and add or remove members. Each change rewrites the team's TEAM.md.

steps.title: Back to the board
steps.body: Click **Board** to return to the team's work. Its number counts the items still open.

steps.title: The work board
steps.body: One column per stage, one card per item with its status, owners and spend. ◆ marks a stage where you decide before an item leaves it. Click a card for its facts, posts, runs and budget.

chapters.title: Agents
chapters.summary: Every Claude Code and Codex agent in one list, shared across hosts

steps.title: Agents on each host
steps.body: Your agents, counted by where they run: on both hosts, Claude Code only or Codex only, plus the ones that come from plugins and Codex's config.toml.

steps.title: Sync now
steps.body: **sync now** refreshes this list and, when sharing is on, copies each host's agents into the other. The tab also asks for a sync when the list is over ten minutes old.

steps.title: Sharing across hosts
steps.body: With both hosts enabled, each host's agents are copied into the other, translated, at the end of every session. When sharing is off, this line says why.

steps.title: Use an agent
steps.body: In Claude Code, ask for an agent by name or type @agent- and its name. In Codex, ask for it by name and Codex spawns it.

steps.title: Filter agents
steps.body: Type to narrow both sections by name, description or plugin.

steps.title: Yours, then the rest
steps.body: Your agents come first, each with a pill per host, its source and whether it is shared; **read-only** marks one whose tools cannot write. Plugin agents and config.toml roles are listed, not copied.

steps.title: Start, copy, open
steps.body: ❯_ opens a new {host} session in Code with the agent, ⧉ copies how to reach it, and **open** opens its file. With sharing on, **unshare** stops copying it to the other host.

chapters.title: Skills
chapters.summary: Every Claude Code and Codex skill in one list, shared across hosts

steps.title: Skills on each host
steps.body: Your skills, counted by where they live: on both hosts, Claude Code only or Codex only, plus those from plugins.

steps.title: Sync now
steps.body: **sync now** refreshes this list and, when sharing is on, copies each host's skills into the other. The tab also asks for a sync when the list is over ten minutes old.

steps.title: Sharing across hosts
steps.body: With both hosts enabled, each host's skills are copied into the other at the end of every session, so a skill made in one is in the other by its next session. When off, this line says why.

steps.title: Filter skills
steps.body: Type to narrow every section by name, description, plugin or program.

steps.title: Yours, then plugins
steps.body: Your skills come first, each with a pill per host, its source and whether it is shared. Plugin skills and built-ins are listed, not copied: they need their plugin's tools.

steps.title: Run, copy, open
steps.body: ❯_ runs the skill in a new {host} session in Code, ⧉ copies how to invoke it, and **open** opens its SKILL.md. With sharing on, **unshare** stops copying it to the other host.

steps.title: MCP servers on each host
steps.body: Each host's MCP servers, a pill per host. **Make available on …** copies one to the other host through that host's own CLI: it shows the exact command, secrets hidden, and the file it writes, backs that file up, and changes nothing until you confirm.

chapters.title: Runs
chapters.summary: Every session and background run, with its cost and full detail

steps.title: Every run
steps.body: **≣ runs** lists the last 50 runs the runtime logged, newest first: your sessions and the jobs that run in the background. It is where you check what ran and whether it worked.

steps.title: Staff roster
steps.body: **⌬ agents** swaps the list for the staff roster: each background agent that keeps a heartbeat, with its last status and summary, when it last ran and runs next, and its last brief.

steps.title: Filter runs
steps.body: Type to narrow the list by run id, what ran or its status: **error** finds the runs that failed. On the roster it filters by name or description.

steps.title: Read the list
steps.body: Each row shows a run's short id, what ran, how long it took, what it cost and how long ago it started. A session's cost is counted once, on its latest run.

steps.title: Open a run
steps.body: Click a run to open its detail beside the list: status, duration, cost, turns, tools, subagents, any error, the prompt and reply, a timeline of events and the raw JSON. ⧉ pops it out.

chapters.title: Settings
chapters.summary: See and change every runtime and app setting in one place

steps.title: Every setting, one tab
steps.body: Settings lists the whole system's settings as the runtime reports them, with how many differ from the defaults. ⌘, opens it from anywhere, and ⟳ reload reads them again.

steps.title: Where values come from
steps.body: A value comes from **this machine** (agenticos.json), **this vault** (brain/config.json) or the default. A change is written to the file that wins, and ↺ on a row puts it back to the default.

steps.title: Master switches
steps.body: Turn whole features on or off: background AI, the Chief of Staff, routines, the knowledge graph, cross-review, costing, telemetry and more. Turning on one that can spend or act on its own asks you first.

steps.title: The local engine
steps.body: Background work runs on the model on this Mac: here is the engine and its address, whether it answers, the model and whether it is downloaded, and today's local calls. **Pull the model** downloads it; each AI feature's own row below says whether it runs here or on a host.

steps.title: One row per setting
steps.body: Each row shows its key, where its value comes from and when a change applies. Pick a value and the runtime checks and saves it; a step left to run shows as a button, counted on the ⚙ badge.

steps.title: Rows for Codex
steps.body: Codex is off on this machine, so its rows are dimmed. You can still set them now; aos init --host both turns Codex on.

steps.title: Rows for Claude Code
steps.body: Claude Code is off on this machine, so its rows are dimmed. You can still set them now; aos init --host both turns Claude Code on.

steps.title: This app's own settings
steps.body: The WORKBENCH rows belong to this app, not the runtime: status bar, poll interval, vault root, config dir, Node binary and terminal defaults. Each saves when you pick it; a few apply after a restart.

steps.title: Hosts and install
steps.body: Hosts, install paths and binaries change only through the installer, so their rows are read-only. ❯_ aos doctor checks the install and ❯_ aos upgrade refreshes the runtime and plugins, in a Code terminal.

steps.title: App settings window
steps.body: App settings (⇧⌘,) opens a separate window. **App** sets the appearance and shows the vault, data folder, write access and versions; **Runtime** has the provider, two system switches and this app's rows.

chapters.title: Status bar
chapters.summary: The line along the bottom: live state and what needs you, one click away

steps.title: The status bar
steps.body: Along the bottom, even with the Workbench closed. **live** means the app is following agent runs as they happen; **idle** means it is not. Click the bar to bring the Workbench back.

steps.title: What needs you
steps.body: Gates, breaking news, alerts, flags, spend near its cap and updates, each opening where it is handled: Agent Teams, Notifications, STATE.md or Settings. aos statusline install shows the same in {host}.

steps.title: Vault health
steps.body: The last vault scan's errors, or its warnings when there are none. Pulse's System health tile lists them, with fixes in its Fix Queue.

chapters.title: Capture and search
chapters.summary: Find anything with ⌘K, capture a memory, and run any command

steps.title: Search everything ⌘K
steps.body: One search over workspace files, memories, runs, agents, skills and Pulse actions. ↵ opens a note, jumps to Runs, or runs the action you picked; ⌘K opens it from anywhere.

steps.title: Quick Capture ⇧⌘M
steps.body: Save a memory without leaving what you are doing: pick its type, write the body, and ⌘↵ files it in brain/memory with its line in MEMORY.md. It is also in the File menu and the menu-bar icon's menu.

steps.title: Every command ⌘P
steps.body: ⌘P has no button: press it anywhere for every command with its shortcut, type to filter and ↵ to run. The menu bar lists them too: the tabs under View, the rest under Commands.

steps.title: Open or search files
steps.body: ⌘O opens any vault file by name. ⇧⌘F opens Files with the cursor in its search box, to find text inside your notes. Both are in the menu bar's File menu.

steps.title: The menu-bar icon
steps.body: The app's icon in the macOS menu bar shows the top items of this status bar, even with the window closed. Click it for the Sidebar HUD; right-click for every item, Open Workbench and Quick Capture…

chapters.title: Help
chapters.summary: Where the tours, What's new and this checklist live

steps.title: The Help menu
steps.body: **Take the tour** replays the welcome tour, **Tour this tab** walks every control on the tab you are on, **What's new** lists each update's changes, and **Documentation** opens the README on GitHub.

steps.title: Getting started
steps.body: Your checklist: a tour for each tab and a few first steps, ticked as you do them. **Hide checklist** puts it away; Help ▸ Getting started brings it back.

steps.title: Moving through a tour
steps.body: → and ← step through a tour, Esc leaves it, and where a step says click, it waits for your click on the highlighted control. The same items are in the app's Help menu and in ⌘P.

actions.title: Run a session with {host}
actions.body: Start {host} in a workspace from Code or Sessions; it is ticked once the runtime logs a session.

actions.title: Review a memory
actions.body: Keep, merge or archive a memory a session wrote, in Brain ▸ Review.

actions.title: Create a routine of your own
actions.body: Schedule a prompt or a command with + new in Routines.

actions.title: Set up your Chief of Staff
actions.body: Run aos persona to create the agent that writes your briefing and files proposals.
